# tracker_write { #wdm.tracker_write }

`tracker_write`

Appending a repeated session to the workout tracker spreadsheet.

Companion to `wdm.exercise`'s read-only estimation. Where
`wdm.exercise.repeat_session_kcal` estimates a repeated session's energy
cost in memory without touching the file, `append_repeated_session`
makes the repetition a permanent, ordinary dated entry -- duplicating the most
recently logged instance of a session, with its exercises, sets, weights,
reps, tempo, equipment-cap flag and its highlight, and notes (including the
hold-duration notes the estimator reads) intact, changed only in date.

This exists because of a mismatch between how the tracker is meant to be used
and how it is actually used. Its own header text says "log every set: date,
exercise, ...", implying a fresh dated block every session -- but a routine
held constant for weeks is more naturally logged once and repeated from
memory, which leaves the file with no row for any session after the first one
of each type. This closes that gap without retyping the block by hand every
time, while keeping the file an honest, growing log rather than a single
template reused forever with no trace of when each session happened.

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [append_repeated_session](#wdm.tracker_write.append_repeated_session) | Append a duplicate of ``session``'s most recently logged block, dated ``as_of``. |

### append_repeated_session { #wdm.tracker_write.append_repeated_session }

```python
tracker_write.append_repeated_session(path, session, as_of, *, backup=True)
```

Append a duplicate of ``session``'s most recently logged block, dated ``as_of``.

Mutates the tracker in place: finds the most recent logged instance of
``session``, inserts an exact copy of its rows immediately before the
sheet's trailing note, with only the date changed. Refuses outright if a
block already exists for ``(session, as_of)``, so running this twice by
accident does not silently duplicate the day.

A ``.bak`` copy is written alongside the file before any modification,
unless ``backup=False``.

Notes are copied verbatim along with everything else. Technique reminders
("rear foot on bench") and hold-duration notes ("1:00 held") carry over
correctly and usefully; day-specific commentary ("last set felt notably
harder") carries over too, and will read as slightly stale until you edit
or clear it by hand. There is no reliable way to tell the two kinds apart
automatically, so this makes no attempt to.

#### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                  | Description                                                                   |
|--------|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|        | (n_rows, source_date) | Number of rows inserted, and the date (``YYYY-MM-DD``) they were copied from. |
